A licensed Swiss chauffeur service — Z-ALS, Kloten
rows.description: Z-ALS was registered in Kloten in 2004 and has worked out of the same airport district ever since. No franchise, no app layer, no subcontracted city fleet.

rows.title: What we actually do — Z-ALS
rows.description: Four service lines, one dispatch desk in Kloten and one Mercedes fleet. The rates below are the published rates; anything outside them is fixed in writing before the journey.

rows.title: Five classes, one standard — Z-ALS
rows.description: You book a class, not a number plate. Every car in it is serviced on schedule at one garage and runs winter tyres from October to April. Choose by passengers and luggage — the standard does not change.

rows.title: One desk, one number — Z-ALS
rows.description: The people who answer the phone are the people who dispatch the cars. Quotes come back in writing within two hours on working days — immediately by phone if you are already travelling.

rows.title: How this work is actually run — Z-ALS
rows.description: Written for the people who buy chauffeur services: travel managers, executive assistants, family offices. Operational detail, pricing logic, and the standards a supplier should be able to evidence.

rows.title: The arrivals gap: what the new border checks did to the walk to the kerb — Z-ALS Journal
rows.description: Biometric registration has put an unpredictable stretch between wheels-down and the arrivals hall. A transfer priced on the old assumption is quoting for a journey that no longer exists.
